summary.title: Toren
summary.pov: Third-person limited (centered on Toren). The narrator observes Rook's deterioration through Toren's eyes and internal calculations.
summary.synopsis: Rook begins to fracture after twenty-six days of vigilance. He makes a tactical error regarding a gate, snaps at Milo for reading him too closely, apologizes awkwardly, and spends the night stabilizing Senna using an artifact called 'the Ember.' The next day, Rook falls asleep in a vulnerable posture during midday rest. That evening, he speaks his dead wife's name ('Vera') while half-asleep. The group realizes Rook is coming apart; they debate whether to wait or intervene. They unanimously decide to push him gently but firmly that night.
summary.openingState: Tired, hyper-vigilant, and internally counting sleepless nights on paper. A sense of dread regarding the 'thing' beginning to come apart.
turningPoints: Rook's tactical error with the gate (Day 26): He creates a gap where there should be none, violating his own training rules.
The confrontation with Milo: Rook snaps at being read/analyzed but then apologizes in an uncharacteristic way ('That was mine and not yours').
Senna's crisis & The Ember: Rook uses the artifact to hold a 'gate' shut for Senna, revealing he is spending something vital on her.
The midday sleep (Day 27): Rook sleeps sitting up with open hands—a sign of total collapse in his usual posture.
The name drop: Rook murmurs 'Vera' and 'the gate' while half-asleep, witnessed by Milo.
The fire council: The group decides to intervene ('push') rather than wait for him to break completely.
summary.closingState: Toren realizes the group has set a trap/line based on Rook's own teachings. He feels horror that they are about to use his mentor against himself, and Milo is terrified of being chosen as the one who must speak.

characters.name: Rook
characters.function: The leader/protector whose mental state is fracturing. He holds 'gates' shut but cannot fix internal damage.
characters.vocalBehavior: Low, flat, and precise when angry; unusually soft and honest during apology; sleep-talking lacks rhythm or shape (flatness). Status: High authority collapsing into vulnerability.

characters.name: Toren
characters.function: Observer/Arithmetician. Tracks the timeline and physical distance.
characters.vocalBehavior: Measured, analytical, internally anxious but externally still. Rhythm is steady until the final realization of horror.

characters.name: Milo Faust
characters.function: The catalyst for conflict; represents the group's curiosity and fear.
characters.vocalBehavior: Grinning initially (light), then sharp/defensive, finally small/horrified. High conversational pressure when asking questions.

characters.name: Dessa
characters.function: The strategist who identifies the fracture and orchestrates the intervention.
characters.vocalBehavior: Direct, commanding but not shouting. Uses 'Right' as a pivot point for serious discussion. Status: Absolute authority.

characters.name: Wyck
characters.function: The moral anchor; provides the psychological framework for Rook's breakdown.
characters.vocalBehavior: Quiet, deliberate, using personal analogy (his mother) to explain Rook's state. Low conversational pressure but high weight.

locations: A lane with a five-bar gate
Midday halt on the road (near a cart and mule)
terms: Stilt: A threat/entity that comes in straight lines.
Drum: An event/location ten days prior where Rook first began to fracture.
Ember: A flat tin artifact used by Rook to stabilize Senna's breathing/condition.
Gate/Gap/Lane: Metaphors for mental barriers and tactical vulnerabilities. 'Holding a gate shut' means suppressing trauma or maintaining order.
summary.actionCadence: Starts with sharp, clipped dialogue (the lane). Slows to internal monologue during the sleep tally. Becomes tense and quiet during Senna's crisis. Shifts to stillness/suspense during Rook's midday collapse. Ends with a slow-burn, heavy conversation around the fire.
summary.emotionalRegister: Suppressed dread, clinical observation, sudden shock (the open hands), deep sorrow (Senna/Vera), and collective resolve mixed with fear of consequences.
narrationRisks: The sleep-talking section ('It's the gate... Vera') must be read as flat, shapeless, and distant. Do not add dramatic inflection; it is a man speaking to no one.
Dessa's opening line 'Right' should feel like a door closing on casual conversation, shifting immediately into high-stakes territory without a pause for breath.
Milo's final reaction ('Oh, *no*') must be delivered with absolute horror and smallness, not melodrama. It is the realization of his own role in the trap.
carryForward: The group has set a 'line' for Rook to cross tonight.
Milo Faust is terrified he will be chosen as the speaker.
Rook knows they are setting this line because it mirrors his own teaching methods.
